A1.justification: Both PDFs describe COMET and contain readable methods, equations, experimental figures, and appendices. The complete 27-page v1 and 30-page v3 support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic routing and neuron-utilization experiments, image-classification and language-modeling results, regression results, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports computational-resource measurements and a CIFAR10-to-SVHN transfer experiment.

M1.justification: The independent fixed routing network, random projections, k-winner-take-all masks, backbone computation, and unmasked output remain unchanged in equations (1)-(8). The new conceptual exposition and proposed future computational optimizations do not change the implemented method.

E1.justification: The seven benchmark datasets and synthetic experiments are retained. Appendix A.10 adds a distinct non-IID transfer scenario: training MLPs on CIFAR10 before fine-tuning on SVHN. This extends task coverage without introducing another dataset.

E2.justification: The ten CIFAR10 comparison methods remain, including both MoE variants, Topk, Bernoulli masking, and example-tied dropout. Other retained experiments use the same standard-model comparators. The new transfer experiment varies pretraining for COMET and the existing standard MLP comparator rather than introducing another competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.10 introduces CIFAR10 pretraining followed by SVHN fine-tuning, with training-on-SVHN-only controls. Appendix A.9 adds evaluation by training hours and GPU memory consumption. Previously reported model configurations, optimizers, training budgets, and hyperparameter experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds two substantive investigations: computational overhead across the vision architectures and controlled cross-task transfer with and without pretraining. These directly examine practical efficiency and transfer beyond within-task generalization, questions not experimentally addressed in v1. Existing routing, utilization, capacity, activation-function, and training-hyperparameter analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Three-seed training and averaging over ten routing networks per synthetic input pair were already documented in v1. The existing uncertainty displays are retained, and v3 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation practice, explicit increase in repeated runs, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Existing experimental plots and scores are retained, but Tables 1-2 and Figure 35 add substantial findings about resource costs and transfer. For example, COMET ViT-Large uses 19.8 versus 12.8 GB, and takes 3.3 versus 1.7 hours on Tiny ImageNet. Figure 35 adds transfer-learning curves with COMET reaching the highest final accuracy. These are new results, not improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: Section 4 adds a mathematical capacity assertion involving O(e^N) approximately orthogonal representations and its implications for interference. The COMET equations, binomial expert count, and NTK derivation remain unchanged. No new proof accompanies the assertion, and its citations appear as unresolved question marks.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies faster learning as faster per update step and specifies out-of-sample generalization. The introduction explicitly distinguishes the single-task focus from conjectured multi-task benefits, while identifying the new transfer test as preliminary. The central COMET contribution and broad performance claims remain.

C2.justification: New discussion acknowledges computational overhead and the unoptimized implementation. Appendix A.10 distinguishes COMET's higher final accuracy from the standard MLP's larger improvement due to pretraining. The conclusion also acknowledges that similar representations and separated activation subspaces can arise naturally in standard networks, refining the interpretation of COMET's advantages.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a COMET repository link, reports training-time and memory requirements, and explicitly discloses that sparse matrix multiplication was not used. This is additional access and implementation information, not evidence of an implementation change. Most architecture, optimizer, hardware, and training details were already present.

R1.justification: v3 expands comparisons with example-tied dropout and model superposition, and more explicitly positions COMET as combining established ideas about masking, routing, and overlapping experts. It removes the Hossain et al. interpretability citation. Several added superposition-related references remain unresolved question marks, limiting attribution.

P1.justification: v3 revises portions of the abstract, introduction, and conclusion; adds the explanatory Section 3; and combines language modeling and regression into one main-text subsection. It also adds acknowledgements and updates affiliation/header text. Most existing method, experiment, and appendix prose is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 1-2 and Figure 35, moves the SVHN and CIFAR10 architecture plots from v1 Figures 5-6 to appendix Figures 10-11, and adjusts a label in Figure 1. Existing result plots are retained, with changes chiefly involving placement, pagination, and conference headers.

improvement.justification: v1 already provides the method and extensive performance and sensitivity evidence. v3 improves transparency by quantifying computational overhead, qualifying the speed claim, adding a controlled transfer experiment, and supplying code-access information. Its acknowledgement that the standard model gains more from pretraining also improves interpretation. These benefits are limited by sparse reporting of the new transfer settings and unresolved citations in the added discussion; the core scientific evidence remains largely unchanged.
